notes: Water-cooled chillers on open cooling towers all year. LBNL: highest WUE of all systems. Physics: 1.48 L evaporated per kWh heat, times heat rejected per kWh IT, times COC/(COC-1).
Elevated chilled water: more waterside economizer hours, but the tower still evaporates. Team assumption: no dry coolers.
Outside air with evaporative assist only on hot hours (above 24 C dry bulb, ASHRAE recommended upper inlet 27 C minus margin). Microsoft fleet WUE 0.27 L/kWh FY25 (Americas 0.34).
18 C facility water: dry coolers only in cold hours (dry bulb at or below supply minus 8 K approach), towers otherwise.
30 C supply: dry coolers at or below 22 C dry bulb, towers or adiabatic trim above. Air share of heat goes through the room system.
32 C supply (Blackwell): dry at or below 24 C dry bulb.
45 C supply (Vera Rubin): dry coolers nearly all year, NVIDIA markets it as chiller free in most climates.
Google liquid-cooled halls with the remaining air share on towers; Google uses evaporative cooling widely.
35 C supply assumed. No source collected.
